basics.title: What this app is
basics.intro1: Tachi Studio is a desk for working with AI. You can chat with it, or point it at a folder and have it build things for you — websites, scripts, small apps — while you watch.
basics.intro2: You do not need to install anything technical or open a terminal. Everything happens inside this window. A few ways in:

ways.chat: Chat — like texting an assistant. Free, no setup.
ways.code: Code — give it a folder + a task, it does real work in that folder.
ways.media: Media — generate images, video, music and voice (and transcribe audio).
ways.nodes: Nodes — wire those steps into a visual workflow and run the whole pipeline.
ways.design: Design — describe a web page or a motion graphic; watch it render live and refine it by chatting.

chat.title: Just chat (the easy start)

steps.type: Type a question at the bottom and press Enter.
steps.done: That is it. The first provider is free and needs no key.

chat.note: It remembers the conversation — ask a follow-up and it knows what you were talking about. Start a fresh topic with New (top right). Each chat keeps its own memory.

extras.commands: Type / to see the command list — /help, /compact, /model, /cost, /memory, /remember, /search, /loop and more. The same slash commands work in Chat, Code, and the HOME "Ask anything" box.
extras.sources: Attach a folder and ask about it — a grounded answer shows Sources chips underneath. Click one to expand the exact file text it used.

code.title: Build things (the Code agent)

steps.choose: Click Choose folder (or drag a folder onto the page). This is the only place the AI is allowed to touch.
steps.type: Type what you want, e.g. "make a simple snake game in an html file", and press the run button.
steps.watch: Watch it work. When it writes a file you can click [PREVIEW] to see it live — an HTML game actually plays right inside the app.

code.note: It can only read and write inside the folder you picked. It cannot wander into the rest of your computer.

extras.tachiapp: Want it to work on its own source? The pinned TACHIAPP row at the bottom of the sidebar opens a Code chat already pointed at Tachi Studio itself — no folder to pick.
extras.spawnLoop: Ask it to split a big task across several agents at once, or type /loop to keep working toward a goal on a repeating interval — a LOOP chip shows it is still running.
extras.incomplete: If a run stops before finishing, you will see an amber ! Ended without completing badge instead of a false "done" — a nudge to keep going or give it more direction.

media.title: Make images, video & music

steps.pick: Pick what to make (image, video, music, speech, transcript), a provider (Surplus or Venice) and a model.
steps.prompt: Type a prompt, optionally drop in a reference image, and press Generate.

media.note: Everything you make is saved in the Artifacts sub-tab. Models that support it can edit an image, or turn one into a video (image-to-video).

buttons.title: What the Code buttons mean
buttons.intro: Four small switches sit at the top of the Code tab. You can ignore them to start — the defaults are fine. Here is what each does:

mode.name: Mode
mode.plain: Plan first, or just build it now

thinking.name: Thinking
thinking.plain: How hard the AI reasons before acting

engine.name: Agent
engine.plain: Which coding agent does the work

gateway.name: Provider
gateway.plain: Where the AI models come from

buttons.note: The [CTX nn%] badge shows how full the AI's memory is. When it turns yellow then red, start a fresh session so it does not forget the early parts.

private.title: Keep it private
private.intro: Private Mode keeps everything on your machine. Cloud AI is blocked, and agents are stopped from reaching the internet at all.

steps.palette: Press Ctrl/Cmd + K to open the command palette.
steps.toggle: Type "Toggle Private Mode" and pick it.
steps.badge: A red [PRIVATE] badge appears at the top. Cloud providers show as [LOCKED].

private.note: In Private Mode only local providers work (Ollama, or llama.cpp). Turn it off the same way to use cloud models again.

providers.title: Connect your own AI (optional)
providers.intro: The free option works with zero setup. To use premium models, add a key:

steps.settings: Go to Settings (bottom of the sidebar) → Providers.
steps.key: Pick a provider, click Get key (opens the signup page), paste the key, click Test.
steps.green: Green means connected. Now you can pick that provider in Chat or Code.

power.title: Power features (when you are ready)

list.nodes: Nodes — draw your own AI pipeline: wire a model to an agent, or chain text → image → video. Every run drops a result card you branch from; pick any model (Venice or local); save and switch flows like chats.
list.swarm: Swarm — run several agents as a team on a shared task board.
list.parallel: Parallel tasks — in Code, run a few agents at once, each in its own copy of the project.
list.inbox: Inbox — instead of a popup for every permission, let requests stack up and approve them in a batch.
list.marketplace: Connections — in Settings → Connections, browse a catalog of MCP tool servers and install one with a single click, no JSON to edit. Private Mode automatically keeps local-only servers running and blocks the rest.
list.scheduler: Scheduled tasks — in Settings → Advanced → Scheduled, set a chat, Code run or flow to fire on a recurring schedule. It survives your machine going to sleep and catches up when it wakes.

power.note: None of these are needed to get value — they are there when you grow into them.

list.palette: Ctrl/Cmd + K — command palette (do anything by typing).
list.new: New — start a fresh chat/session with a clean memory.
list.tooltip: Hover any button — a tooltip explains it in plain words.
list.reconnect: If a reply stalls, watch for a Retrying n/10 banner — the connection dropped and is reconnecting itself into the same reply. No need to resend; just wait it out.

design.title: Design — build a page or animation

steps.pick: Pick page (a static web page → export PNG/PDF) or animate (a motion graphic → export MP4).
steps.engine: In animate mode, choose a renderer: Remotion (renders to an MP4 video) or HyperFrames (an HTML + GSAP animation).
steps.type: Type what you want ("a pricing page with three tiers", "a logo that spins in"). It renders on the right; keep chatting to change it.

design.note: Everything auto-saves to a folder on disk, and you can click any text in a page preview to edit it in place. Export buttons are top-right.

footer.deepDocs: Want the deep technical version? The full architecture and per-feature docs live in docs/app/ inside the project — the in-app agent can read them to understand and extend Tachi Studio itself.
